terms.gloss: catch in the act, catch red-handed
evidence: Cic. Clu. 20: cum manifestō venēnum dēprehendisset (Lewis & Short s.v. manifestus)
terms.comment: Manifestō, “plainly, in the act”; of the culprit himself, manifestus, caught in the act (Lewis & Short).
The legal phrase of later centuries, “while the offence is blazing”; Lewis & Short has no such phrase, so Cicero’s manifestō is recommended.

sources: Lewis & Short: manifestus · Lewis & Short: deprehendo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 95, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
